title: The Construction Worker Whose Belly Filled With Fluid — Jaundice, Sepsis, and Alcohol Withdrawal

sections.heading: The Patient's Story
sections.content:
He is 49 years old, a construction worker, presenting with abdominal distension, breathlessness on exertion, fever, and yellowing of his eyes for the past 15 days, along with vomiting for a week and loose stools for 12 days that eventually settled with medication.

He had been apparently well 15 days before this, when he developed fever, vomiting, and loose stools, for which he took medication from a local practitioner. There was no improvement over 3–4 days. He then developed abdominal distension, breathlessness on exertion, and mild swelling in his feet, prompting a visit to a hospital in Miryalaguda, where he was diagnosed with alcoholic liver disease complicated by sepsis and acute kidney injury, with a positive hepatitis B surface antigen, and started on treatment there. His vomiting had been bilious, non-projectile, mixed with food particles, occurring once or twice a day for four days before settling with medication. He also experienced whole-body shivering attributed to alcohol withdrawal, high-grade intermittent fever with chills, and watery, foul-smelling loose stools two to three times a day that also settled with medication. From there he was brought to this hospital for further evaluation and treatment.

He has no history of hypertension, diabetes, asthma, epilepsy, coronary artery disease, or tuberculosis. He had surgery for multiple rib fractures four years ago, with a blood transfusion at that time. He eats a mixed diet, has had decreased appetite, and has regular bowel and bladder habits, with no known allergies. He has been a known alcoholic for 20 years, drinking 180 ml daily.

sections.heading: What the Work-Up Showed So Far
sections.content:
- **General exam:** conscious, coherent, and cooperative; icterus present; no pallor, cyanosis, clubbing, generalized lymphadenopathy, or edema
- **Vitals:** blood pressure 80/60 mmHg, pulse 80 bpm, temperature 98°F, oxygen saturation 98%
- **Abdominal exam:** distended abdomen without visible scars, sinuses, or engorged veins; non-tender with free fluid present and shifting dullness; liver palpable, spleen not palpable; bowel sounds present
- **Systemic exam:** heart sounds S1 and S2 normal; bilateral air entry present; no abnormality detected on neurological exam
- **Serology:** positive hepatitis B surface antigen

sections.heading: How the Story Unfolded on the Ward
sections.content: He was diagnosed with alcoholic liver disease complicated by acute kidney injury and sepsis, in the setting of chronic hepatitis B infection. Over a 16-day admission, his treatment was adjusted in stages: the first week focused on thiamine and B-complex supplementation for his alcohol use history, broad-spectrum antibiotic coverage (piperacillin-tazobactam) for his sepsis, and a short tapering course of lorazepam alongside nicotine replacement gum to manage alcohol and tobacco withdrawal. From day 8 he was transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin and lactulose syrup for hepatic symptom control, and by days 12–16 his regimen had been simplified further to lactulose, a multivitamin, and continued nicotine replacement as needed.
